authorities.name: R v Woollin
authorities.date_note: Year only confirmed (1998); an earlier version of this entry asserted a specific day/month ('22 July') that was not actually reported by the verifying agent - it was added during transcription without a source and has been corrected rather than left uncaught.
authorities.proposition: A jury is not entitled to find the intention necessary for murder unless sure that death or serious bodily harm was a virtual certainty, barring some unforeseen intervention, as a result of the defendant's actions, and that the defendant appreciated that was the case - refining the earlier R v Nedrick test for oblique intent.
authorities.verification_note: Not read directly - BAILII blocked (HTTP 403), block treated as final. Quoted verbatim within R v Royle [2013] EWCA Crim 1461 (below), fetched live.

authorities.name: R v Royle
authorities.date_note: Year only confirmed via the citation itself; exact date not independently verified this session.
authorities.proposition: Measures a trial judge's jury direction against the Woollin/Nedrick standard, quoting Woollin's virtual-certainty formulation directly at para 17 and treating it as current binding authority fifteen years on.

edges.verified_via: R v Royle [2013] EWCA Crim 1461, para 17, fetched directly from Find Case Law: quotes and applies the Woollin virtual-certainty test.

what_this_is_not: One verified node-pair confirming Woollin's virtual-certainty test for oblique intent remains good law as of 2013. Does not independently confirm Woollin's original 1998 text - see verification_note above - and does not survey the wider law on intention for murder beyond this single point.
